Could it wait until tomorrow?
It's New Year's. They've tried in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city.
Docent is unlikely to find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the cottage!
Oh, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply. It's addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have dinner with us on New Year's Day?
- We promise!
451:
It's a shame. Such a nice woman,
and her father's a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all this noise? Who said you could go out?
- There he is. The bad man.
454:
The New Year is here. I hope
this year brings each of you a new beginning.
455:
Anything may happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... One moment...
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of? He says
he'll find us anywhere and slit our throats.
461:
They say he took a razor to Speckled's throat—
slice, and that was that. - He's gone savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to visit? Father Frost!
And he's brought you presents!
463:
- Come here, Fedya. - What have I done?
- Come on. Wear these. They're slippers.
464:
- What do I need slippers for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. There's time.
465:
- And they'll be useful in prison for now. Wear them.
- Always predicting the worst.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
And this is yours, Gavrila Petrovich. - Thanks.
467:
- Pure wool.
- And this is for you too.
469: Too sour. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Must you get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and have
a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I don't do heart-to-hearts.
- We could play a game.
473:
You must think I'm a sucker!
You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you start with its last letter:
"Washington." You'd start with N. Got it?
477: Your turn, Fedya. A city beginning with N.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Fine. Yours must begin with A.
- Dzhambul. - Why Dzhambul?
480:
Because it's warm there.
My home is there. My mother too.
481:
Let's play this instead. I'll go out,
you hide something, and I'll find it.
482:
- You'd do better finding our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it and he'll peek through a crack?
- No. You go out and hide it, then.
484:
And you watch so I don't peek.
- Why me? It's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth off, you little wretch!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- You came on your own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried your place,
but sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry to call you out for nothing, doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him some valerian drops,
warm tea, and let him sleep. - Thanks.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It does, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, we found out
you're in prison,
500:
and we're very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
Who told that little Weasel
about his father?
502:
"Mom was happy too. When your letter came,
she cried all day,
503:
though she used to say
you were a test pilot."
505:
"I'm still glad you're alive,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good man,
but easily led."
507:
Exactly! So easily led, he stole
our money and blamed the taxi driver.
508:
Beat it! I'll knock your horns off,
you rotten radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed? You're forty.
Half your lives are over.
511:
What's behind you? What have you now?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, nothing decent!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
513:
Listen, Docent. We should get out.
That doctor will report us.
514:
- She won't. - Why?
- I took a razor to her throat.
515:
She's in the well.
Take a look if you like.
516:
What was my sentence?
One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
And I'm supposed to put up
with that snake for a measly fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old woman in the well?
Do what you like. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on. He won't touch you.
523:
And you? Are you going to put up with him
until you're dead?
524:
Vasya, I told him I had a cold earlier,
and he...
525:
Enough about your cold!
Come here.
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades, the show's over.
First, I'm taking this off.
530:
Once I've served my time, that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? - Watchman on my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could clear snow, lay bricks,
or translate. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought back helmet!
Docent is crook.
534:
- Many crooks. Only one helmet.
- They'd reduce our sentences for it.
535:
Where did he put it?
We looked everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was, "Rip your mouth off."
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
"I'll fish, you dive."
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing through a hole in the ice."
540:
- Then he asked if I could swim.
- He hid the helmet in that hole!
541:
That's it! I remember! The bad man!
In the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you oaf?
Could've left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Leave him for them. I'm not carrying that hog. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing in there.
- It's at the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? It's always Squint.
Vasya, tell him to dive himself.
547:
I can't! It's cold.
I'll get sick.
548:
- You were hanging yourself just now, and now you're afraid of a cold?
- A sporty hello!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551:
I'd kill you all,
but I haven't got time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another back at the cottage.
555:
- Two.
- The more we bring in, the better.
